lessons.title: Separate path components
lessons.about: Split-Path extracts parent paths, leaf names, qualifiers, and other components without manual string splitting.
lessons.example_output: reports
breakdown: The input is a relative Windows path.
-Parent returns everything above the leaf name.
lessons.task: Print the parent portion of reports\daily.txt.
hints: Request the -Parent component.

checks.description: The parent path was printed.

lessons.completion: Split-Path understands provider syntax and is safer than splitting on backslashes.

lessons.title: Convert to a provider-native path
lessons.about: Convert-Path converts an existing PowerShell provider path into its native path representation.
lessons.example_output: C:\work\note.txt
breakdown: The input item must exist.
The result is a plain native path string.
lessons.task: Print the native absolute path to note.txt.
hints: Pass the existing relative file path.

checks.description: The native file path was printed.

lessons.completion: Resolve-Path returns PathInfo objects; Convert-Path returns native path strings.

lessons.title: List PowerShell drives
lessons.about: Get-PSDrive lists logical drives exposed by providers, including file systems, variables, functions, aliases, and the registry.
lessons.example_output:
Name Used (GB) Free (GB) Provider   Root
---- --------- --------- --------   ----
C                        FileSystem C:\
breakdown: -PSProvider filters by provider type.
File-system drive names can be used like normal PowerShell locations.
lessons.task: Print the name of the first file-system PowerShell drive.
hints: Filter to FileSystem and select the first Name.

checks.description: A file-system drive name was printed.

lessons.completion: PowerShell drives provide a consistent navigation model across different data stores.

lessons.title: Inspect available providers
lessons.about: Get-PSProvider lists the engines that expose data stores through PowerShell's drive and path model.
breakdown: Providers define path semantics and capabilities.
Each provider can expose one or more PowerShell drives.
lessons.task: Print the names of all providers available in this Windows PowerShell session.
hints: Expand the Name property.

checks.description: The FileSystem provider was listed.
The Registry provider was listed.

lessons.completion: Providers explain why familiar cmdlets can work with more than files.

lessons.title: Read item properties
lessons.about: Get-ItemProperty retrieves properties stored on provider items and returns them as PowerShell object properties.
lessons.example_output:
Length : 6
Name   : note.txt
breakdown: The file-system provider returns FileInfo-like metadata.
Select-Object can isolate one property value.
lessons.task: Print only the byte length property of note.txt.
hints: Expand the Length property.

checks.description: The six-byte length was printed.

lessons.completion: Get-ItemProperty reads provider metadata without parsing formatted listings.

lessons.title: Create a ZIP archive
lessons.about: Compress-Archive packages files and directories into a standard ZIP archive without an external utility.
breakdown: -Path selects the source directory.
-DestinationPath names the ZIP file.
lessons.task: Create evidence.zip from the evidence directory.
hints: Provide both source and destination paths.

checks.description: The ZIP archive was created.

lessons.completion: Compress-Archive creates ZIP files; verify the source selection before archiving sensitive data.

lessons.title: Extract a ZIP archive
lessons.about: Expand-Archive extracts ZIP contents into a destination directory using native PowerShell cmdlets.
breakdown: The ZIP path is the source.
-DestinationPath controls where contents appear.
lessons.task: Create bundle.zip from note.txt, then extract it into restored.
lessons.solution: Compress-Archive note.txt bundle.zip; Expand-Archive bundle.zip restored
hints: Create the ZIP first, then expand it into restored.

checks.description: The restored file contains the original text.

lessons.completion: Archive extraction stays inside the disposable workspace for this rep.

lessons.title: Serialize objects as CLI XML
lessons.about: Export-Clixml preserves PowerShell object properties and type information in PowerShell's XML serialization format.
breakdown: Pipeline objects supply the serialized records.
The output file is designed for Import-Clixml.
lessons.task: Serialize the objects in people.csv to people.xml.
hints: Import the CSV, then pipe objects to Export-Clixml.

checks.description: The CLI XML file was created.

lessons.completion: CLI XML is PowerShell-specific and retains more object metadata than plain CSV.

lessons.title: Restore serialized PowerShell objects
lessons.about: Import-Clixml reconstructs deserialized PowerShell objects from files created in the CLI XML format.
lessons.example_output:
Name
----
alpha
breakdown: The XML file contains serialized property data.
The restored object exposes its Name property.
lessons.task: Import data.xml and print only its Name property.
hints: Import the file, then expand Name.

checks.description: The restored Name property was printed.

lessons.completion: Imported CLI XML objects are deserialized snapshots rather than live original instances.

lessons.title: Inspect access control information
lessons.about: Get-Acl retrieves the security descriptor and access-control information for a local file or directory.
lessons.example_output:
Path Owner Access
---- ----- ------
note.txt ...   ...
breakdown: The path stays inside the practice directory.
Owner and Access are structured properties.
lessons.task: Print only the owner recorded on note.txt.
hints: Expand the Owner property.

checks.description: A file owner was printed.

lessons.completion: Get-Acl is read-only; review access rules carefully before applying changes.

lessons.title: Inspect running processes
lessons.about: Get-Process returns live process objects containing identifiers, resource measurements, names, and other metadata.
lessons.example_output:
Handles NPM(K) PM(K) WS(K) CPU(s) Id ProcessName
------- ------ ----- ----- ------ -- -----------
...                         ... 1234 powershell
breakdown: $PID identifies this PowerShell process.
The result is a Process object.
lessons.task: Print only the name of the current PowerShell process.
hints: Query -Id $PID and expand ProcessName.

checks.description: The current process name was printed.

lessons.completion: Get-Process is read-only; process objects can be filtered before any deliberate action.

lessons.title: Preview stopping a process
lessons.about: Stop-Process terminates processes, so this rep requires -WhatIf and only previews the action against its own process.
lessons.example_output: What if: Performing the operation Stop-Process...
breakdown: $PID selects only the current PowerShell process.
-WhatIf prevents the termination.
lessons.task: Preview stopping the current PowerShell process without actually stopping it.
hints: The rep requires the -WhatIf safety switch.

checks.description: The protected preview completed successfully.

lessons.completion: Use -WhatIf to review destructive process selections before acting.

lessons.title: Pause a script briefly
lessons.about: Start-Sleep pauses the current PowerShell process for a specified interval without consuming a busy loop.
breakdown: -Milliseconds accepts short intervals.
A successful pause emits no output.
lessons.task: Pause this disposable process for 10 milliseconds.
hints: Use the -Milliseconds parameter.

checks.description: The short pause completed successfully.

lessons.completion: Start-Sleep is useful for polling intervals and controlled retry timing.

lessons.title: Inspect Windows services
lessons.about: Get-Service returns ServiceController objects describing installed Windows services and their current states.
lessons.example_output:
Status Name     DisplayName
------ ----     -----------
Running EventLog Windows Event Log
breakdown: EventLog selects one stable Windows service.
Status and Name remain structured properties.
lessons.task: Print only the service name for Windows Event Log.
hints: Query EventLog and expand Name.

checks.description: The EventLog service name was printed.

lessons.completion: Get-Service is read-only and is the safe first step before any service decision.

lessons.title: Preview starting a service
lessons.about: Start-Service changes service state, so this rep permits only a -WhatIf preview against the EventLog service.
lessons.example_output: What if: Performing the operation Start-Service...
breakdown: The service is selected by its stable name.
-WhatIf prevents any state change.
lessons.task: Preview starting EventLog without changing the service.
hints: Include the required -WhatIf switch.

checks.description: The protected start preview completed.

lessons.completion: Preview service changes first, especially when dependencies and production workloads are involved.

lessons.title: Preview stopping a service
lessons.about: Stop-Service changes service state, so this rep requires -WhatIf and cannot stop the Windows Event Log service.
lessons.example_output: What if: Performing the operation Stop-Service...
breakdown: EventLog names the target service.
-WhatIf guarantees a preview only.
lessons.task: Preview stopping EventLog without changing it.
hints: Use the mandatory -WhatIf switch.

checks.description: The protected stop preview completed.

lessons.completion: Service stops can affect many consumers; inspect dependencies and preview the selection.

lessons.title: Preview restarting a service
lessons.about: Restart-Service combines a stop and start, so this rep permits only a -WhatIf preview and makes no host change.
lessons.example_output: What if: Performing the operation Restart-Service...
breakdown: EventLog is the selected service.
-WhatIf prevents the restart.
lessons.task: Preview restarting EventLog without changing it.
hints: The safety boundary requires -WhatIf.

checks.description: The protected restart preview completed.

lessons.completion: A restart is an outage, however brief; preview and understand the impact first.

lessons.title: Discover available modules
lessons.about: Get-Module inspects modules loaded in the session or installed on the module search path.
lessons.example_output:
ModuleType Version Name
---------- ------- ----
Manifest   3.1.0.0 Microsoft.PowerShell.Utility
breakdown: -ListAvailable searches installed modules.
The name narrows the result to a built-in module.
lessons.task: Print the name of the installed Microsoft.PowerShell.Utility module.
hints: Use -ListAvailable, then select the first Name.

checks.description: The built-in utility module name was printed.

lessons.completion: Modules package commands and can be discovered before they are imported.

lessons.title: Load a built-in module
lessons.about: Import-Module loads commands from a module into the current PowerShell session; this rep allows only a built-in module.
lessons.example_output:
ModuleType Version Name
---------- ------- ----
Manifest   3.1.0.0 Microsoft.PowerShell.Utility
breakdown: The module name resolves through PSModulePath.
-PassThru returns the loaded module object.
lessons.task: Import Microsoft.PowerShell.Utility and print its name.
hints: Use -PassThru, then expand Name.

checks.description: The imported built-in module name was printed.

lessons.completion: Import only trusted modules and review their source and scope before use.

lessons.title: Measure execution time
lessons.about: Measure-Command times a local expression and returns a TimeSpan describing its elapsed duration.
lessons.example_output: Ticks : 1234
breakdown: The script block contains a static local expression.
The result is a TimeSpan object.
lessons.task: Measure the static expression 1 + 1 and print only elapsed ticks.
hints: Measure the expression, then expand Ticks.

checks.description: A non-negative tick count was printed.

lessons.completion: Measure-Command is useful for coarse comparisons; repeat measurements before drawing conclusions.

lessons.title: Create and format dates
lessons.about: Get-Date retrieves the current time or parses a supplied date into a DateTime object that can be formatted and compared.
breakdown: The supplied value makes the result deterministic.
-Format controls the output text.
lessons.task: Format the supplied date 2000-01-02 as yyyy-MM-dd.
hints: Use the exact custom date format.

checks.description: The deterministic date was formatted correctly.

lessons.completion: Keep DateTime objects structured until the final presentation or serialization step.

lessons.title: Calculate elapsed time
lessons.about: New-TimeSpan creates a TimeSpan from explicit endpoints or duration components.
lessons.example_output: Days : 2
breakdown: -Start supplies the first DateTime.
-End supplies the later DateTime.
lessons.task: Print the total days between 2026-01-01 and 2026-01-03.
hints: Expand the TotalDays property.

checks.description: The two-day interval was printed.

lessons.completion: TimeSpan properties make durations easier to compare than formatted strings.

lessons.title: Select a random input object
lessons.about: Get-Random returns random numbers or randomly selects objects supplied through -InputObject.
lessons.example_output: green
breakdown: -InputObject supplies the candidate collection.
One candidate is returned by default.
lessons.task: Select from an input collection containing only the number 7.
hints: A one-item input makes the result deterministic.

checks.description: The only candidate value was returned.

lessons.completion: Get-Random is convenient for sampling, but security-sensitive randomness needs threat-specific review.

lessons.title: Inspect regional settings
lessons.about: Get-Culture returns the current culture object used for formatting numbers, dates, currencies, and comparisons.
lessons.example_output:
LCID Name  DisplayName
---- ----  -----------
1033 en-US English (United States)
breakdown: Name is the culture identifier.
Other properties describe formatting conventions.
lessons.task: Print only the current culture name.
hints: Expand the Name property.

checks.description: The current culture name was printed.

lessons.completion: Culture affects parsing and formatting, so automation should make expectations explicit.

lessons.title: Inspect the PowerShell host
lessons.about: Get-Host returns information about the application hosting the PowerShell engine, including its version and capabilities.
lessons.example_output:
Name : ConsoleHost
Version : 5.1...
breakdown: The host is separate from the operating system.
Version identifies the PowerShell host version.
lessons.task: Print the current host version as dotted text.
hints: Expand Version, then call its safe ToString member through ForEach-Object.

checks.description: A dotted PowerShell host version was printed.

lessons.completion: Host and engine versions help explain feature and behavior differences between environments.

lessons.title: Query CIM system information
lessons.about: Get-CimInstance queries Windows management data and returns structured CIM instances without screen scraping.
lessons.example_output:
SystemDirectory Organization BuildNumber RegisteredUser SerialNumber Version
...
breakdown: Win32_OperatingSystem names a CIM class.
The result exposes system properties as object members.
lessons.task: Print only the operating-system caption from CIM.
hints: Query the class, then expand Caption.

checks.description: A Windows operating-system caption was printed.

lessons.completion: CIM queries are a structured foundation for Windows inventory and diagnostics.

lessons.title: Collect broad computer information
lessons.about: Get-ComputerInfo aggregates operating-system, hardware, firmware, and configuration details into one large object.
lessons.example_output:
WindowsProductName
------------------
Windows Server 2022 Datacenter
breakdown: Get-ComputerInfo can be relatively expensive.
Select-Object narrows the broad object early.
lessons.task: Print only the Windows product name.
hints: Expand WindowsProductName from the result.

checks.description: A Windows product name was printed.

lessons.completion: Select only the properties you need from broad inventory commands.

lessons.title: List installed Windows updates
lessons.about: Get-HotFix reads installed update records and returns identifiers, descriptions, installation dates, and related metadata.
lessons.example_output:
Source Description HotFixID InstalledBy InstalledOn
------ ----------- -------- ----------- -----------
...
breakdown: The command is read-only.
The first record is sufficient for a short inventory rep.
lessons.task: Print the HotFixID of the first installed update record.
hints: Select the first record and expand HotFixID.

checks.description: A Windows update identifier was printed.

lessons.completion: Update inventory is one signal; support status and deployment policy require additional context.

lessons.title: Inspect physical disks
lessons.about: Get-Disk returns Windows disk objects with numbers, sizes, partition styles, health, and operational status.
lessons.example_output:
Number Friendly Name Serial Number HealthStatus OperationalStatus Total Size Partition Style
------ ------------- ------------- ------------ ----------------- ---------- ---------------
0      ...                         Healthy      Online            ...        GPT
breakdown: Disk numbers identify storage devices in management cmdlets.
This rep performs read-only inspection.
lessons.task: Print the number of the first disk Windows reports.
hints: Select the first disk and expand Number.

checks.description: A numeric disk identifier was printed.

lessons.completion: Disk operations can be destructive; begin with read-only inventory and verify identifiers carefully.

lessons.title: Inspect mounted volumes
lessons.about: Get-Volume returns volume objects with drive letters, labels, file systems, sizes, and health state.
lessons.example_output:
DriveLetter FriendlyName FileSystemType DriveType HealthStatus SizeRemaining Size
----------- ------------ -------------- --------- ------------ ------------- ----
C                        NTFS           Fixed     Healthy      ...           ...
breakdown: Volumes are distinct from physical disks.
DriveLetter can be null for unlettered volumes.
lessons.task: Print the first non-empty drive letter.
hints: Filter out null DriveLetter values before selecting the first.

checks.description: A drive letter was printed.

lessons.completion: Volumes expose file systems and capacity; disks represent underlying storage devices.

lessons.title: Inspect assigned IP addresses
lessons.about: Get-NetIPAddress returns structured address assignments across Windows network interfaces.
lessons.example_output:
IPAddress InterfaceIndex InterfaceAlias AddressFamily Type PrefixLength PrefixOrigin SuffixOrigin AddressState PolicyStore
...
breakdown: -AddressFamily narrows the query to IPv4.
Each result includes address and interface properties.
lessons.task: Print the first IPv4 address Windows reports.
hints: Filter by IPv4 and expand IPAddress.

checks.description: An IPv4 address was printed.

lessons.completion: Address objects retain interface, prefix, origin, and state information for later filtering.

lessons.title: Summarize interface configuration
lessons.about: Get-NetIPConfiguration summarizes adapters, IP addresses, gateways, and DNS servers as related objects.
lessons.example_output:
InterfaceAlias : Ethernet
InterfaceIndex : 4
IPv4Address    : 10.0.0.5
IPv4DefaultGateway : ...
DNSServer : ...
breakdown: Each object represents one interface configuration.
InterfaceAlias is a human-readable adapter name.
lessons.task: Print the alias of the first configured network interface.
hints: Select the first object and expand InterfaceAlias.

checks.description: A network interface alias was printed.

lessons.completion: Use the related address, gateway, and DNS properties instead of parsing ipconfig text.

lessons.title: Inspect network adapters
lessons.about: Get-NetAdapter returns physical and virtual network adapter objects with status, speed, names, and interface details.
lessons.example_output:
Name InterfaceDescription ifIndex Status MacAddress LinkSpeed
---- -------------------- ------- ------ ---------- ---------
Ethernet ...              4       Up     ...        10 Gbps
breakdown: Status identifies whether the adapter is operational.
Name is suitable for later adapter cmdlets.
lessons.task: Print the name of the first network adapter.
hints: Select the first adapter and expand Name.

checks.description: A network adapter name was printed.

lessons.completion: Adapter inventory is read-only here; changing adapters can disconnect a machine.

lessons.title: Inspect the routing table
lessons.about: Get-NetRoute returns Windows routing entries as objects with destinations, next hops, metrics, and interfaces.
lessons.example_output:
ifIndex DestinationPrefix NextHop RouteMetric ifMetric PolicyStore
------- ----------------- ------- ----------- -------- -----------
...
breakdown: -AddressFamily narrows the route set.
DestinationPrefix represents a routed network.
lessons.task: Print the first IPv4 destination prefix.
hints: Expand DestinationPrefix from the first IPv4 route.

checks.description: An IPv4 destination prefix was printed.

lessons.completion: Route objects can be filtered by interface, destination, and metric without parsing columns.

lessons.title: Inspect TCP endpoints
lessons.about: Get-NetTCPConnection returns local TCP listeners and connections with addresses, ports, state, and owning process identifiers.
lessons.example_output:
LocalAddress LocalPort RemoteAddress RemotePort State OwningProcess
------------ --------- ------------- ---------- ----- -------------
0.0.0.0      135       0.0.0.0       0          Listen ...
breakdown: -State Listen narrows the collection.
OwningProcess can be correlated with Get-Process.
lessons.task: Print the state of the first listening TCP endpoint.
hints: Query listening endpoints and expand State.

checks.description: A listening endpoint reported Listen.

lessons.completion: Connection objects preserve ports, addresses, states, and owning process IDs for correlation.

lessons.title: Test loopback reachability
lessons.about: Test-Connection sends ICMP echo requests and returns response objects; this rep is restricted to the local loopback name.
lessons.example_output:
Source Destination IPV4Address IPV6Address Bytes Time(ms)
------ ----------- ----------- ----------- ----- --------
...    localhost   127.0.0.1               32    0
breakdown: localhost keeps traffic on this machine.
-Count 1 performs one short probe.
lessons.task: Send one loopback probe and print its Address property.
hints: Use localhost and -Count 1, then expand Address.

checks.description: The loopback response address was printed.

lessons.completion: A successful echo confirms only this narrow path, not application availability.

lessons.title: Resolve the local host name
lessons.about: Resolve-DnsName performs structured DNS queries; this offline rep is limited to the local host name.
lessons.example_output:
Name Type TTL Section IPAddress
---- ---- --- ------- ---------
localhost A   ... Answer 127.0.0.1
breakdown: localhost avoids an external DNS dependency.
Returned records expose names, types, and addresses.
lessons.task: Resolve localhost and print the first record's Name property.
hints: Resolve only localhost, then expand Name.

checks.description: The local host name was resolved.

lessons.completion: Structured DNS records are easier to filter by record type than nslookup display text.

lessons.title: Inspect script execution policy
lessons.about: Get-ExecutionPolicy reports the effective PowerShell script execution policy without changing it.
lessons.example_output: RemoteSigned
breakdown: The result is the effective policy name.
-List can show policy by scope.
lessons.task: Print the effective execution policy for this process.
hints: No parameters are needed for the effective policy.

checks.description: An execution policy name was printed.

lessons.completion: Execution policy is a safety feature, not a complete security boundary.

lessons.title: Inspect a script signature
lessons.about: Get-AuthenticodeSignature reports whether a Windows file has a valid Authenticode signature and exposes signer details.
lessons.example_output:
SignerCertificate Status    StatusMessage Path
----------------- ------    ------------- ----
                  NotSigned ...           script.ps1
breakdown: The synthetic script is intentionally unsigned.
Status is a structured enumeration value.
lessons.task: Print only the signature status of note.ps1.
hints: Expand the Status property.

checks.description: The unsigned script reported NotSigned.

lessons.completion: A valid signature identifies integrity and signer context; trust decisions still require policy.

lessons.title: Copy a local access-control descriptor
lessons.about: Set-Acl applies a security descriptor to a path; this rep copies one between synthetic files inside the disposable workspace.
breakdown: Get-Acl supplies the source security descriptor.
Set-Acl applies it only to the local target file.
lessons.task: Apply reference.txt's access-control descriptor to target.txt.
hints: Pipe the reference ACL directly into Set-Acl for the target.

checks.description: The local ACL copy completed successfully.
The target file content was not changed.

lessons.completion: ACL changes can remove access; always capture and review the intended descriptor first.

lessons.title: List local user accounts
lessons.about: Get-LocalUser returns local Windows account objects with names, enabled state, descriptions, and account metadata.
lessons.example_output:
Name Enabled Description
---- ------- -----------
Administrator False Built-in account...
breakdown: The command reads the local account database.
Account state remains a structured property.
lessons.task: Print the name of the first local user account.
hints: Select the first account and expand Name.

checks.description: A local user account name was printed.

lessons.completion: This rep inventories accounts only; creating or changing accounts is outside its boundary.

lessons.title: List local groups
lessons.about: Get-LocalGroup returns local Windows security group objects and their descriptions.
lessons.example_output:
Name Description
---- -----------
Administrators Administrators have complete and unrestricted access...
breakdown: The local group database is queried read-only.
Names can be passed to membership cmdlets.
lessons.task: Print the name of the first local security group.
hints: Select the first group and expand Name.

checks.description: A local group name was printed.

lessons.completion: Group inventory is read-only here; membership changes require deliberate authorization.

lessons.title: Inspect local group membership
lessons.about: Get-LocalGroupMember lists users and groups contained in a local Windows security group.
lessons.example_output:
ObjectClass Name                      PrincipalSource
----------- ----                      ---------------
User        HOST\Administrator        Local
breakdown: Administrators is a stable built-in group.
ObjectClass distinguishes users from nested groups.
lessons.task: Print the object class of the first Administrators group member.
hints: Select the first member and expand ObjectClass.

checks.description: A group member object class was printed.

lessons.completion: Membership inspection is a key step before reviewing local privilege assignments.

lessons.title: Inspect scheduled tasks
lessons.about: Get-ScheduledTask returns registered Windows task definitions with names, paths, states, actions, triggers, and principals.
lessons.example_output:
TaskPath TaskName State
-------- -------- -----
\       ...      Ready
breakdown: The command reads Task Scheduler registrations.
TaskName and TaskPath identify each definition.
lessons.task: Print the name of the first registered scheduled task.
hints: Select the first task and expand TaskName.

checks.description: A scheduled task name was printed.

lessons.completion: This rep performs task inventory only and does not register, start, or remove tasks.

lessons.title: Query modern Windows event logs
lessons.about: Get-WinEvent queries classic and modern Windows event logs and returns structured event and log metadata objects.
lessons.example_output:
LogMode MaximumSizeInBytes RecordCount LogName
------- ------------------ ----------- -------
Circular ...               ...         Application
breakdown: -ListLog requests log metadata rather than event records.
Application is a standard local log.
lessons.task: Print the LogName for the local Application event log.
hints: Use -ListLog Application and expand LogName.

checks.description: The Application log name was printed.

lessons.completion: Get-WinEvent supports structured filtering that scales better than reading every event.

lessons.title: List classic event logs
lessons.about: Get-EventLog reads classic Windows event logs and remains useful on Windows PowerShell for legacy workflows.
lessons.example_output:
Max(K) Retain OverflowAction Entries Log
------ ------ -------------- ------- ---
...    ...    OverwriteOlder ...     Application
breakdown: -List returns classic log containers.
The Log property contains each log name.
lessons.task: Print the name of the first classic Windows event log.
hints: Use -List, then expand Log from the first result.

checks.description: A classic event log name was printed.

lessons.completion: Get-WinEvent is preferred for newer event channels and richer filtering.

lessons.title: Run a local script block
lessons.about: Invoke-Command can execute script blocks locally or through remoting; this rep permits only a static local arithmetic expression.
breakdown: No computer or session parameter is supplied.
The script block contains only static arithmetic.
lessons.task: Use a local script block to calculate 2 + 3.
hints: Use -ScriptBlock with the static expression.

checks.description: The local expression returned five.

lessons.completion: Real remoting requires explicit authorization, trusted endpoints, authentication, and network controls.

lessons.title: Enable stricter script rules
lessons.about: Set-StrictMode makes common scripting mistakes fail earlier, including references to uninitialized variables and invalid properties.
breakdown: -Version Latest enables all current strict checks.
The setting affects only this disposable scope.
lessons.task: Enable the latest strict-mode rules for this PowerShell process.
hints: Use -Version Latest.

checks.description: Strict mode was enabled successfully.

lessons.completion: Strict mode catches many mistakes early and belongs near the start of reusable scripts.

lessons.title: Query legacy WMI data
lessons.about: Get-WmiObject queries Windows Management Instrumentation and appears in many existing Windows PowerShell scripts.
lessons.example_output:
SystemDirectory Organization BuildNumber RegisteredUser SerialNumber Version
...
breakdown: Win32_OperatingSystem names the WMI class.
The result exposes system properties as an object.
lessons.task: Print the operating-system caption from legacy WMI.
hints: Query the operating-system class and expand Caption.

checks.description: A Windows operating-system caption was printed.

lessons.completion: Prefer CIM cmdlets for new automation while recognizing WMI in established Windows PowerShell code.

lessons.title: Inspect the Windows time zone
lessons.about: Get-TimeZone returns the current Windows time-zone object with its identifier, display name, offset, and daylight rules.
lessons.example_output:
Id : Pacific Standard Time
DisplayName : (UTC-08:00) Pacific Time...
breakdown: Id is the stable Windows time-zone identifier.
Other properties describe offsets and daylight support.
lessons.task: Print only the current Windows time-zone identifier.
hints: Expand the Id property.

checks.description: The Windows time-zone identifier was printed.

lessons.completion: Time-zone context is essential when comparing timestamps across systems and logs.
